g.text: Speculative Decoding with Provable Latency and Lossless Verification
Julian Richter, Maya Lin, Aris Thorne, Sunita Deshmukh

Julian Richter, Maya Lin, Aris Thorne, Sunita Deshmukh
Speculative decoding accelerates large language model (LLM) generation by employing a lightweight draft model to
hypothesize sequences of candidate tokens, followed by parallel verification under the target foundation model.
However, standard speculative decoding faces severe tail-latency bottlenecks under distribution drift, and heuristic
tree search introduces unbounded verification latency. Here we introduce MartingaleTree, an exact speculative decodin…
Large language models (LLMs) underpin transformative advances in reasoning and code generation, but their
interactive deployment is severely constrained by memory bandwidth limitations . Autoregressive token generation
loads all model weights into high-bandwidth memory for every token produced, resulting in low arithmetic intensity…
Speculative decoding was pioneered by Leviathan et al. and Chen et al. , demonstrating that modified rejection
sampling guarantees exact distribution equivalence. Subsequent works expanded linear speculation into tree
structures (SpecInfer , Medusa, EAGLE). However, these architectures rely on heuristic branch pruning based on
static confidence thresholds, which fail to adapt to dynamic token entropy and lead to tail latency spikes.…
Let p(x_t x<t) and q(x_t x<t) denote target and draft distributions over vocabulary V. Candidates are verified via
rejection sampling r_i = (1, p(x_i)/q(x_i)) with residual sampling pres(x) = (0, p(x)-q(x))1 - Σ_y (p(y), q(y)),
ensuring DTV(Pspec, Ptgt) 0. Along any candidate branch, the likelihood ratio M_k = j=1^k p(xt+j)q(xt+j) forms a
non-negative martingale with E[M_k] = 1. By Ville's inequality, P(1 ≤ k ≤ K M_k ≥ λ) ≤ 1/λ. We construct stopping…
We evaluate MartingaleTree using Llama-3-70B-Instruct as the target foundation model and Llama-3-1. 5B as the draft
model on 8× NVIDIA H100 SXM5 GPUs. Benchmarking spans MT-Bench (multi-turn conversation), GSM8K (mathematical
reasoning), and HumanEval (code synthesis) across 5 independent seeds.
Ablation experiments confirm that Martingale stopping eliminates tail latency spikes without sacrificing throughput.
Compared to unconstrained tree search, 99th-percentile token latency is reduced from 48. 6 ms to 18. 2 ms. •
Acceptance-Rejection: Each token accepted with probability (1,q/p), preserving exact target distribution. •…
